arc: Vic's six tickets cannot leave his phone and Vic will be at his daughter's wedding, so the phone has to travel without him; after seventy-five days of typing Danny sends four words, "Leave it with me." (Episode 5). Danny leaves the phone with the one person who always gets there, his grandmother, who is not in the chat and will not answer it because it is not her phone, so the group spends the rest of the season asking Danny for tickets he no longer holds (Short A). Maya books seven seats and four people fly: Vic is at a wedding, Lee found it cheaper in nineteen hours, Danny is "to be confirmed", and the six tickets are still at home in a floral armchair (Episode 6). The kick-off time is finally confirmed in green and moved the next moment for television, to a time that suits only Sydney, who is not going, and that turns Lee's cheap route into an arrival at half-time (Short B). On match day the grandmother, who likes to be early, is in her seat with Danny behind her and Vic's phone ringing on her lap ("That'll be for Vic."), while the four who did everything properly stand at the gate and learn where their tickets are from Sydney, who has seen her on television. The season ends where last season did, at greater expense and with everyone content: two got in, one is not in the chat and the other is typing; Lee arrives at half-time having missed nothing, Vic pays on a Friday and the chip moves for the first time, Jo's verdict is "It was fine.", the last stamp reads CONFIRMED, and the grandmother's status is WENT.

films.moves: Everything is settled. Who got in: Danny and his grandmother, as last season. Vic's six tickets entered the ground on his phone, on her lap, unanswered. Jo, who never said yes, came. why:
Why this continuation. It is driven by the three mechanics Episode 4 left on the table. The ticket on a phone that cannot be sent on forces the phone to travel. The wedding removes its owner, which also quietly solves "one short": six tickets, six going. The journey splits a booking of seven into four, each absence a type every travelling fan knows. Each film ends on a question the next one answers: what will Danny do; who can reach the phone; will tickets that travel on the day arrive; what does a lunchtime kick-off do to them; who gets in.

Every thread from the first six films is paid off except one.
- Danny's typing: "Leave it with me.", then typing again to the last frame.
- Tickets on Vic's phone: they get in, on the grandmother's lap.
- The wedding: Vic never looked at his phone, and his record goes to attended 11, bought 25.
- Jo: she came without ever saying yes, and "Should be fine" becomes the verdict "It was fine."
- OWE MAYA: 6: Vic pays on a Friday and the chip reads 5.
- Lee: his cheaper route arrives at half-time, "What did I miss?" / "Nothing."
- Sydney: the new time suits only him, and he finds the tickets on television.
- The kick-off time: confirmed in green, then moved, with Lee's unused "Again."
- The grandmother: paper ticket, likes to be early, WENT.
- The series title: the last stamp reads CONFIRMED and the last line returns it to "to be confirmed".
- Not paid off: the Elsewhere man. I treated his short as closed by its own ARRIVED stamp.

The ending replays Episode 1's "Two arrived. Neither was in the chat." one notch drier, so the season closes on its own premise. The group is wrong about the day, the time, Vic, Jo, Danny and the tickets, and content anyway.

Limits. Narration is 275 of 700 characters in seven lines; people, the chat and paperwork carry the rest. There are 8 new shots of 10, with one extra still for Vic in a suit, which leaves two for retakes or for the Elsewhere man. Lengths are 32.9, 18.9, 27.6, 19.5 and 34.1 seconds. No new kind of graphic is used.

Biggest risk. The finale leaves the four who did everything properly outside the ground. If "Nothing." and "It was fine." are played with any self-pity, or if Danny reads as having abandoned them rather than simply being Danny, the ending turns sour and Maya becomes the fool the bible forbids. It needs flat performances and the full silence after each line. It also depends on a viewer connecting the humming phone to the six tickets, which is why Short A spends its one narrator line on exactly that.

Smaller risks.
- Episode 7 is 0.9 s under the ceiling with nine beats. If the real takes run long, shorten Vic's hold first and never the stamp's silence.
- Episode 6 is 1.6 s over the floor.
- Short B opens on the same frame as Episode 4. That is deliberate, since the same thing is happening again, but it could look like a repost for two seconds.
- G2 asks for a phone humming on a lap in a roaring stand, the hardest shot to get clean. If it fails, she can hold the phone as she does at home.
